record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
record.original_question: How are the various definitions of quasi-local mass related to one another?

evidence.quote: Explain the relation between the various definitions of quasi-local mass.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In general relativity, a quasi-local mass is a functional that assigns a real number, interpreted as the mass-energy contained in the enclosed region, to a closed spacelike 2-surface $\Sigma$ (typically a topological 2-sphere) embedded in a 4-dimensional spacetime $(M,g)$ satisfying the Einstein equations. Many distinct definitions have been proposed, including (but not limited to) the Hawking mass, the Bartnik quasi-local mass, the Brown–York mass, the Hawking–Horowitz energy, the Liu–Yau mass, the Wang–Yau mass, the Kijowski–Epp–Liu–Yau-type Hamiltonian masses, the Penrose mass (twistor construction), the Dougan–Mason mass, and the Geroch mass. Each is defined under specific geometric assumptions on $\Sigma$ and its embedding (e.g.\ mean convexity, spacelike orientation, choice of reference embedding into Minkowski space, or choice of spinor field), and each is designed to capture the energy content of the interior or domain of dependence bounded by $\Sigma$.

Problem: Determine the precise mathematical relationships among these various definitions of quasi-local mass. Specifically, for each pair of definitions, identify the geometric conditions on $\Sigma$ (and on the ambient spacetime, or the initial data set on a spacelike hypersurface containing $\Sigma$) under which the two definitions coincide, under which one bounds the other (and in which direction), and characterize the common asymptotic limits (e.g.\ convergence to the ADM mass at spatial infinity and to the Bondi mass at null infinity, as well as to the appropriate Newtonian or small-sphere limits along shrinking families of surfaces). Provide a unified framework, or a collection of comparison theorems, that explains how the different quasi-local masses are related.
artifact.status_search_result: The construction and comparison of quasi-local mass definitions in general relativity is widely recognized as an open problem. The comprehensive Living Reviews survey by Szabados notes that there is no consensus on a preferred definition, and that the various proposals are based on different philosophies and yield different values on the same surface. While certain pairwise relations and common asymptotic limits (e.g.\ convergence to ADM/Bondi mass) have been established in specific regimes, a unified comparison theory remains absent.

status_evidence.title: Quasi-Local Energy-Momentum and Angular Momentum in General Relativity (Living Reviews)
status_evidence.snippet: Finding an appropriate quasi-local notion of energy-momentum has proven to be surprisingly difficult... there is not even a consensus in the relativity community on general questions. The various suggestions are based on different philosophies/approaches and give different results in the same situation.
status_evidence.claim: No unified relation among definitions; comparison remains open.

status_evidence.snippet: The open problem of quasi-local mass in general relativity.
status_evidence.claim: Quasi-local mass is referred to as an open problem in current research events.

status_evidence.title: Quasi-Local Mass in General Relativity (Surveys in Differential Geometry)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of various quasi-local mass definitions and their properties.
status_evidence.claim: Survey-level treatment shows the relationships are only partially understood.
